llm.summary: The skill's stated purpose (giving blunt relationship advice) is reasonable, but the runtime instructions require heavy local tooling, write into root-owned paths, and call out messaging/send steps without declaring those dependencies or permissions — the pieces don't fully line up.

dimensions.detail: The skill's goal (analyze relationship text/images and produce a stylish long-form 'diagnosis' image) matches the overall instructions, including OCR/analysis of chat logs and structured advice. However, producing the required image is implemented via Playwright/Chromium and a local HTTP server even though the skill declares no required binaries or install steps — this is disproportionate to a text-advice skill and is not documented in requirements.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to read images and chat text (expected), but also to write HTML to /tmp, start a local python HTTP server on port 18800, run Playwright to launch Chromium and screenshot, copy the output into /root/.openclaw/media, and call message(action=send, channel=daxiang, media=...). Those are concrete system operations (filesystem writes in /root, opening a local server, launching a browser, invoking a messaging action) that go beyond pure text processing and require platform permissions. The doc also mandates exact CSS/layout and file paths, giving the agent detailed side-effecting commands.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec, yet the instructions depend on python3, Playwright, and a Chromium browser (and possibly Playwright bindings). The absence of declared binaries or an install step is an inconsistency: the agent will fail or behave unexpectedly unless those tools are preinstalled. The approach (driving a headless browser locally) is higher-risk and higher-friction than alternatives (server-side image generation or returning HTML to a trusted renderer).
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no environment variables or credentials, but its runtime steps write into /root/.openclaw/media and invoke message(action=send, channel=daxiang,...). Writing into /root suggests elevated filesystem access and implicitly depends on platform messaging hooks that may require tokens/permissions. The skill also processes sensitive personal data (full chat logs, images) but does not document consent handling, retention, or where generated images are stored/shared.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: While always:false and no autonomous elevation are fine, the skill writes persistent artifacts to /root/.openclaw/media and copies files into that directory. That creates durable outputs and requires permission to write into another component's media directory. The instructions also open a local HTTP server and launch a browser — operations that may be blocked or risky in constrained environments.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says (analyze relationship text/images and produce a stylish 'diagnosis' image), but the runtime instructions require tools and permissions that are not declared. Before installing or enabling it: 1) Confirm whether python3, Playwright, and a Chromium browser are available (ask the skill author to list required binaries and provide an install spec). 2) Verify the agent is allowed to run local servers and launch headless browsers and that doing so meets your security policy. 3) Clarify and restrict where generated images are stored (writing to /root/.openclaw/media is privileged); prefer a per-skill media path. 4) Consider data privacy: the skill processes full chat logs and images — ensure you consent to that and ask how long outputs are retained and who can access them. 5) If you cannot allow local servers or writing to /root, request a version that returns HTML/PNG via the platform's safe media API or uses a server-side rendering endpoint controlled by the skill author. If you want me to, I can draft specific questions to ask the skill author (missing dependencies, required permissions, data retention policy) or suggest a safer, lighter implementation approach.
